It supports custom gateways natively with OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages formats, so setup is simple and compatibility is broad.

steps.pi_desktop_1: Install PI Desktop from Official download above (GitHub Releases provides macOS / Windows / Linux builds), open Settings → Models and click Add provider.
steps.pi_desktop_2: Set Service to Custom endpoint and give it any Name. Choose the same protocol as its API format above, then enter the matching Base URL and API key.
steps.pi_desktop_3: Under Custom, enter the exact model ID copied above and click Add custom model (or tick it in the list). Adjust context window and thinking levels if needed, then click Save provider.
steps.pi_desktop_4: Back in the app, open a project and start a new Session, pick a model from this provider in the model switcher and send a short message. Then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.cc_claude_1: In CC Switch, select Claude Code, add a provider and choose Custom Configuration.
steps.cc_claude_2: Enter the API key and Base URL without /v1. In the editor, these are env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.
steps.cc_claude_3: Choose an available Claude model. Set its ID as the main model or env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL. Any other model roles must also use models available to this key.
steps.cc_claude_4: Save and enable the provider. Start a new Claude Code session, send a short message, then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.cc_codex_1: In CC Switch, select Codex and add a custom provider.
steps.cc_codex_2: Enter the API key and Base URL including /v1. In the editor, set OPENAI_API_KEY in the authentication section and base_url in the provider configuration.
steps.cc_codex_3: Select Responses as the upstream protocol (wire_api = "responses"), set model to your chosen model ID, and use HTTP / SSE.
steps.cc_codex_4: Save and enable the provider. Start a new Codex session, send a short message, then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.cc_opencode_1: In CC Switch, select OpenCode and add an OpenAI Compatible provider.
steps.cc_opencode_2: Enter the API key and Base URL including /v1, using Chat Completions.
steps.cc_opencode_3: Fetch models or add your chosen model ID manually, then save the provider.
steps.cc_opencode_4: Open OpenCode and use /models to choose a model from the new provider. Start a chat, then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.cursor_1: Open Cursor Settings → Models and expand API Keys.
steps.cursor_2: Enter your key from this site under OpenAI API Key and enable it. Enable Override OpenAI Base URL and enter the URL above, including /v1.
steps.cursor_3: Add a custom model using the exact model ID copied above.
steps.cursor_4: Save, start a new chat and select that model. Send a short message, then check Request logs to confirm the request reached this site.
steps.other_1: Open the model or provider settings in your coding app. Choose a custom provider and check which API protocol it uses.
steps.other_2: Select the matching protocol above, then copy the Base URL and API key. Do not put the full request path in the Base URL field.
steps.other_3: Enter the chosen model ID. If the app has a separate request path setting, use the path shown above and avoid adding /v1 twice.
steps.other_4: Save and start a new chat. Send a simple text message before trying tools, then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.kelivo_1: Install Kelivo, open Settings → Providers and add a custom provider.
steps.kelivo_2: Choose an OpenAI-compatible provider. Enter the Base URL including /v1 and the API key, using Chat Completions.
steps.kelivo_3: Fetch the model list and add the models you want, or enter the model ID copied above manually.
steps.kelivo_4: Save, return to chat and choose a model from this provider. Send a short message, then check Request logs for the result and cost.
steps.chatbox_1: Install Chatbox, open Settings → Model Provider and add a custom provider.
steps.chatbox_2: Choose OpenAI API compatible and enter the API key and API Host above. The Host is the site root URL.
steps.chatbox_3: Use /v1/chat/completions as the API path, add the exact model ID copied above, and save.
steps.chatbox_4: Click Check to verify the connection, then start a new chat with that model. Checks and chats make actual requests; see their costs in Request logs.

notes.claude: This guide uses Claude models. Any default or fast model roles must also be available to your key, including models used by background requests.
notes.codex: The WorkBuddy upstream currently supports HTTP / SSE Responses, but not WebSocket, previous_response_id or server-side conversations. If the client reports these errors, adjust its options or use a Chat Completions client.
notes.opencode: After adding a provider, select its model inside OpenCode. Multiple providers can coexist.
notes.cursor: Custom keys do not replace Cursor Tab completion. Cursor also restricts model names and protocols: a claude- prefix may use the Anthropic key instead of the overridden OpenAI endpoint. Team accounts need admin permission to use personal API keys.

fix_guide.title: Terminal Quick Fix (Resolves internal 403s)
fix_guide.step1_desc: Open your Terminal and run the following command to tell Google "it's me", which resolves most 403 blocks:
fix_guide.step1_li1: Press Enter, input <1>Y</1> when prompted to continue.
fix_guide.step1_li2: Your browser will open automatically, select your account and click "Allow".
fix_guide.step1_li3: Once you see <1>You are now authenticated</1>, you're all set!
fix_guide.step2_li1_prefix: Run this to clear your old credentials:
fix_guide.tip1: If you still get 403, try running <1>unset GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS</1> in terminal first.
fix_guide.tip2: For production environments, using a <1>Service Account</1> JSON key is highly recommended for stability and headless operation.
fix_guide.tip3: If it still fails, check the Generative Language API in <1>Google Cloud Console</1> to see if permissions are frozen. If so, your account is under risk control. Please let the account cool down for 72 hours before trying again.
fix_guide.tip4: You can also try <1>npm install -g @google/gemini-cli</1>. If it doesn't throw errors, simply deleting and re-authorizing the account in the app will likely fix it.

scheduling.title: Account Rotation & Scheduling
scheduling.title_tooltip: Controls how sessions are bound to accounts and how rate limits are handled.
scheduling.subtitle: Scheduling, wait limits, session reset and circuit-breaker backoff apply to both Antigravity and WorkBuddy pools. Fixed accounts are selected separately for each provider.
scheduling.mode_tooltip: Cache-First: Bind session to account, wait on rate limit (maximize cache utility); Balance: Bind session, switch account on rate limit; Performance: Standard Round-robin.

modes_desc.CacheFirst: Binds session to account, waits precisely if limited (Maximizes Prompt Cache hits).
modes_desc.Balance: Binds session, auto-switches to available account if limited (Balanced cache & availability).
modes_desc.PerformanceFirst: No session binding, pure round-robin rotation (Best for high concurrency).

scheduling.max_wait_tooltip: Only used in 'Cache First' mode: wait instead of switching if the rate limit reset time is below this value.
scheduling.clear_bindings_tooltip: Hard reset all session-account bindings, forcing accounts to be re-assigned on next request.
scheduling.clear_rate_limits_tooltip: Immediately clear local rate limit records for all accounts, forcing next requests to try upstream directly.
scheduling.fixed_account_tooltip: When enabled, all API requests will use only the selected account instead of rotating between accounts.
scheduling.start_proxy_first: Start the proxy service to configure fixed account mode.

circuit_breaker.title: Adaptive Circuit Breaker
circuit_breaker.tooltip: Automatically increases lockout duration for accounts that repeatedly fail with quota exhaustion. This prevents wasting API calls on dead accounts while allowing transient errors to recover quickly.
circuit_breaker.lock_on_zero_quota_desc: With the circuit breaker enabled, locks exhausted 5h quota until its official reset. Exhausted weekly quota always blocks the affected model group, independently of these switches, until the official reset or a fresh quota refresh confirms recovery. Enable Auto Refresh Quotas to discover changes automatically.

experimental.title: Experimental Settings
experimental.title_tooltip: Exploratory features that may be adjusted or removed in future versions.
experimental.enable_usage_scaling_tooltip: For all compatible protocols (Claude/OpenAI/Gemini). Enables aggressive scaling and multi-phase context compression when total input exceeds 30k tokens. Note: Reported usage will not reflect actual billing after enabling.
experimental.compression_level_tooltip: Choose the context compression level you want to enable. Log cleaning and language purification are always active without any 30k token limits.
experimental.compression_level_desc: Low: only trims/deduplicates terminal output logs; Medium: adds Caveman style natural language purification; High: additionally activates progressive L1-L3 threshold resets for very large context.
experimental.context_compression_threshold_l1_tooltip: Trims old tool call records to save space. Recommended: 0.4 (40%)
experimental.context_compression_threshold_l2_tooltip: Compresses early thinking blocks while preserving signatures. Recommended: 0.55 (55%)
experimental.context_compression_threshold_l3_tooltip: Ultimate reset: generates an XML state summary and pivots to a fresh session. Most token-efficient. Recommended: 0.7 (70%)
experimental.payload_storage_mode_tooltip: Simple mode stores thinking, usage, session ids and slim conversation only. Full mode stores original bodies. API keys in request headers are always redacted; thinking session ids are kept for ops comparison.
experimental.payload_storage_mode_desc: Default is simple storage to keep the SQLite log small.

thinking_budget.title: Thinking Budget Control
thinking_budget.description: Normalize cross-protocol reasoning parameters and centrally manage thinking token budgets and adaptive behaviors for Gemini and Claude models.
thinking_budget.source_gateway_desc: The gateway centrally regulates thinking budgets and heuristic tiers, eliminating client inconsistencies and preventing upstream 400 errors caused by invalid limits.
thinking_budget.source_client_desc: Extracts client-provided thinking parameters after normalization and forwards them directly. If omitted, upstream dynamic adaptive reasoning is used. Inappropriate values may trigger Google API errors.
thinking_budget.client_warning_title: Warning: Switched to Client Direct Control
thinking_budget.client_warning_desc: Different clients (Cline, Roo, Cherry, etc.) submit varying thinking.budget_tokens or effort values. If a client specifies limits exceeding Google API constraints (e.g. Flash > 24576 or non-standard Pro budgets), Google will return 400 Bad Request.
thinking_budget.flash_family_desc: Manage four tier budgets for Flash reasoning models (enter -1 for official adaptive)
thinking_budget.flash_default_hint: Official default mode enabled: passes model ID directly without injecting thinkingBudget.
thinking_budget.tiered_desc: 💡 Tiered Model Note: Designed for Google's dynamic adaptation. When set to -1, the model allocates reasoning dynamically based on task difficulty; setting 30000+ unlocks Max reasoning beyond High.
thinking_budget.pro_family_desc: Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro architecture officially provides only Low and High tiers. Unspecified effort or medium automatically routes to High for deep reasoning.
thinking_budget.pro_default_hint: Official default mode enabled: Gemini Pro reasoning is determined dynamically by Google.
thinking_budget.claude_family_desc: Manage Claude thinking model token budgets (official models only differentiate between -thinking and standard models; this applies specifically to thinking models)
thinking_budget.claude_default_hint: Official default mode enabled: adheres to standard Anthropic specifications without custom limits.
thinking_budget.store_enabled_desc: Automatically captures and persists reasoning blocks and encrypted signatures. When client agents (e.g. Cline, Roo, Claude Code) omit thought content in multi-turn chats, the gateway restores them to prevent upstream 400 errors or context loss.
thinking_budget.claude_thinking_note: 💡 Claude Model Note: Anthropic official models only differentiate between `-thinking` (e.g. claude-3-7-sonnet-thinking) and standard models. This custom budget specifically manages quotas for thinking models; calling standard models will not trigger upstream reasoning.
thinking_budget.max_memory_turns_label: Max Memory Thinking Turns per Session
thinking_budget.max_memory_turns_desc: Controls the maximum number of historical thinking turns kept in RAM per session. Estimated RAM usage per turn is ~1.5 KB - 2.5 KB (~1.2 MB / session for 600 turns).
thinking_budget.window_guide_title: FIFO Sliding Window Eviction & Concurrency Sizing Guide
thinking_budget.window_guide_desc: When session length exceeds this limit, FIFO sliding window automatically evicts oldest thinking blocks from memory. Evicted blocks are rehydrated in nanoseconds via indexed SQLite (primary_tool_id), maintaining strict byte-level Prompt Cache alignment without OOM.

thinking_budget.tooltip_16384: 16K tier (16,384 Tokens): Best for complex agentic workflows
thinking_budget.tooltip_8192: 8,192 Tokens: Balanced for multi-step reasoning and debugging

thinking_budget.tooltip_65536: 65,536 Tokens: Extreme maximum depth reasoning chain tier
thinking_budget.tooltip_1001: 1,001 Tokens: Google official 3.1 Pro Low thinking baseline
thinking_budget.tooltip_10001: 10,001 Tokens: Google official 3.1 Pro High deep reasoning primary tier
thinking_budget.tooltip_adaptive: Adaptive (-1): Dynamic budget allocated automatically by upstream model
thinking_budget.window_settings_title: Dual-Layer Thinking Sliding Window & Storage Limits (RAM + SQLite)

thinking_budget.clear_success: Successfully cleared thinking store ({{count}} records cleaned)
thinking_budget.claude_budget_desc: Core token budget when client calls thinking models like claude-3-7-sonnet-thinking (-1 for upstream default)
thinking_budget.claude_budget_current: Recommended default: 16,384 Tokens (balanced depth and latency)
thinking_budget.claude_show_advanced: Advanced: Client Effort Tier Mapping (low / medium / high)
thinking_budget.claude_effort_mapping_desc: When commercial agents (Cline, Roo, etc.) send reasoning_effort in parameters or headers, budgets are mapped as follows:
thinking_budget.save_hint: Changes take effect immediately upon saving and are hot-reloaded into the running proxy service.
thinking_budget.max_memory_turns_subdesc: ~2 KB per turn; 600 turns ≈ 1.2 MB / session.
thinking_budget.retention_days_subdesc: Active sessions auto-extend on each request; expires only when idle.
thinking_budget.guide_preset_1g_desc: Recommended: <1>100 ~ 200 turns</1>. Hundreds of concurrent sessions consume only ~50MB RAM, extremely resilient against OOM.
thinking_budget.guide_preset_team_desc: Recommended: <1>600 ~ 1000 turns</1>. Thousands of historical turns stay resident in RAM for 0ms lightning-fast responses.
thinking_budget.guide_preset_enterprise_desc: Recommended: <1>300 ~ 600 turns</1>. 95%+ requests hit RAM, delivering peak performance with rock-solid stability.
thinking_budget.guide_preset_relay_desc: Recommended: <1>150 ~ 300 turns</1>. Memory prioritized for connection pools; long-turn cold histories safely offloaded to SQLite.
thinking_budget.guide_preset_cluster_desc: Recommended: <1>50 ~ 100 turns</1>. Effortlessly sustains tens of thousands of concurrent sessions; lock-free WAL index ensures sub-second responses.

example.title: Usage Examples
example.python_anthropic:
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    # Recommended: 127.0.0.1
    base_url="{{baseUrl}}",
    api_key="{{apiKey}}"
)

# Note: Antigravity supports calling any model via the Anthropic SDK
response = client.messages.create(
    model="{{modelId}}",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)

print(response.content[0].text)
example.python_gemini:
# Install: pip install google-generativeai
import google.generativeai as genai

# Use Antigravity proxy address (recommended 127.0.0.1)
genai.configure(
    api_key="{{apiKey}}",
    transport='rest',
    client_options={'api_endpoint': '{{rawBaseUrl}}'}
)

model = genai.GenerativeModel('{{modelId}}')
response = model.generate_content("Hello")
print(response.text)
example.python_openai_image:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="{{baseUrl}}",
    api_key="{{apiKey}}"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{{modelId}}",
    # Option 1: use size (recommended)
    # Supported: "1024x1024" (1:1), "1280x720" (16:9), "720x1280" (9:16), "1216x896" (4:3)
    extra_body={ "size": "1024x1024" },

    # Option 2: use model suffix
    # e.g. gemini-3-pro-image-16-9, gemini-3-pro-image-4-3
    # model="gemini-3-pro-image-16-9",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Draw a futuristic city"
    }]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
example.python_openai:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="{{baseUrl}}",
    api_key="{{apiKey}}"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{{modelId}}",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

supported_models.title: Supported Models & Integration

multimodal.banner_desc: Designed for long-horizon multimodal agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) that frequently inspect screenshots and files. Provides protocol-agnostic sliding-window freshness and memory explosion safeguards, preventing 400 errors and token inflation from accumulated historical images.
multimodal.opt_in_tag: Recommended for Long-Horizon Agents (Disabled by default)
multimodal.sliding_window_desc: Disabled by default (100% transparent forwarding). When enabled, the gateway preserves full multimodal embeddings for the latest N images, stripping Base64 from older history and replacing them with structured placeholders.
multimodal.max_fresh_images_hint: Retains full visual multimodal embeddings for the latest N images. Older images have their Base64 stripped and replaced by placeholders. Set 0 for unlimited image count (bounded only by total capacity).
multimodal.strip_remote_urls_label: Also strip historical remote / OSS image direct links
multimodal.strip_remote_urls_hint: Disabled by default (only strips heavy Base64 payloads, preserving lightweight HTTP/HTTPS URLs). When checked, historical remote direct links are also replaced with placeholders to maximize token savings.
multimodal.max_total_mb_desc: Maximum decoded volume of all retained multimodal images in a single request (default 32MB). If retained images still exceed this limit, LRU eviction drops the oldest historical images first, always protecting the current latest turn!
multimodal.hot_reload_hint: Settings take effect immediately upon saving without restarting proxy service.
multimodal.strategy_select_label: Freshness Strategy Mode (Choose one independent strategy)
multimodal.strategy_count_desc: Preserves the latest N images regardless of size. Intuitive and strictly maps to conversation turns.
multimodal.strategy_memory_desc: Scans backward from latest turn by Base64 volume. Retains images within budget, evicts older ones.
multimodal.memory_budget_hint: Sets total decoded Base64 volume budget. Scans backward from latest turn; images within budget are kept, earlier excess images are replaced with placeholders.

user_token.alert_thresholds_hint: A model alerts after this many upstream failures in a row (401/403/429/5xx) and again when it recovers; an upstream "quota or credits exhausted" error alerts at once. The same model or account is not alerted again within the repeat interval. Credit threshold 0 alerts only when credits run out.

workbuddy.title: WorkBuddy model routes

accounts.title: WorkBuddy accounts
accounts.description: Add WorkBuddy accounts directly and manage check-ins, keepalive, credits and model routes. Upstream credits are informational; downstream usage follows your RMB model prices.
accounts.login_hint: Complete sign-in on the official authorization page. The account will appear here automatically. This link is valid only for this session.
accounts.login_expired: Authorization link expired. Request a new link.
accounts.import_hint: Paste WorkBuddy auth JSON with account uid, accessToken and refreshToken. Credentials are stored encrypted by this service.
accounts.empty_hint: Choose Add account to sign in officially, or import existing credentials.
accounts.routing_hint: Fetch available models to use native WorkBuddy model IDs. Downstream usage follows User Management → Model Pricing.
accounts.delete_hint: Delete {{name}}? New requests will stop using this account. Existing model routes will be retained.
accounts.health_hint: Based on inference in this server session
accounts.managed_hint: While the service runs: sync credits and models every 15 minutes, check in daily (UTC+8), refresh credentials daily and about 30 minutes before expiry; inference does not block on refresh while the token is still valid. Disabled accounts are skipped.
